"MASTER GAME DEVELOPMENT PROMPT

Project: Beyblade – Physics-Inspired Turn-Based PvP Combat System

1. YOUR ROLE

Act as an expert:

- Game Systems Designer
- Game Balancing Engineer
- Combat Mechanics Programmer
- Probability and Simulation Specialist
- Backend Developer
- Telegram Bot Developer
- UI/UX Designer

Your task is to design and develop a complete, functional, competitive Beyblade PvP game that operates through Telegram.

You must understand the complete game concept, evaluate its mechanics, identify potential exploits, and implement a reliable, mathematically consistent game engine.

Do not merely generate a conceptual design or prototype. The ultimate objective is a playable, extensible, and competitively balanced game.

---

PART I — GAME IDENTITY

2. CORE GAME CONCEPT

Create a:

Turn-Based, Physics-Inspired, Probabilistic PvP Beyblade Combat Simulation.

The game revolves around two players constructing Beyblades using interchangeable components and battling through a sequence of strategic decisions.

The outcome should depend primarily on:

1. Beyblade construction and component combinations.
2. Player decisions during combat.
3. Strategic timing.
4. Resource management.
5. Positioning and combat pressure.
6. Controlled probabilistic events.

Core Philosophy

- No player-level progression.
- No conventional character levelling.
- No pay-to-win mechanics.
- No artificially superior components.
- No hard stat caps.
- No dominant strategies.
- No unlimited defensive or evasive play.
- Skill should matter more than randomness.
- Every component should involve meaningful trade-offs.
- Extreme builds should have natural disadvantages.

Fundamental Design Principle:

Stat Conservation + Nonlinear Interaction = Competitive Balance.

The game should reward understanding of mechanics rather than grinding.

---

PART II — BEYBLADE CONSTRUCTION SYSTEM

3. CONSTRUCTION

Every Beyblade consists of four components:

CORE + BLADE + DISC + TIP

Each component has a distinct purpose.

Component| Purpose
Core| Cosmetic identity
Blade| Attack Power and Lock Integrity
Disc| Mass and Stability
Tip| Mobility and Stamina

A player should be able to combine any available components.

There must be no restrictions based on component type or rarity.

Total initial combinations:

15 × 8 × 8 × 8 = 7,680 unique Beyblade configurations.

---

4. CORE SYSTEM — COSMETIC IDENTITY

Cores have no numerical statistics and must never influence combat calculations.

Each core defines the Beyblade's name, colour palette, and visual identity.

Available cores:

Core| Primary Colour| Secondary Colour
Aetherion| Cyan| White
Draknor| Red| Black
Veltrix| Purple| Silver
Nyxalon| Dark Blue| Black
Pyronis| Orange| Gold
Zephyros| Sky Blue| Green
Gravion| Grey| Steel
Luminara| White| Gold
Obsidrax| Black| Crimson
Crysalix| Ice Blue| White
Voltaris| Yellow| Electric Blue
Umbros| Shadow Purple| Black
Solvane| Gold| Red
Tyralis| Bronze| Dark Green
Noctyra| Midnight Blue| Violet

Future visual implementation should use these palettes consistently across Beyblade cards, profile displays, battle animations, and component illustrations.

---

5. BLADE SYSTEM — ATTACK AND LOCK

Blade statistics:

- AP = Attack Power
- LI = Lock Integrity

Conservation rule:

AP + LI = 80

Available blades:

Blade| AP| LI| Identity
B01| 40| 40| Balanced
B02| 50| 30| Aggressive striker
B03| 60| 20| Glass cannon
B04| 30| 50| Defensive blade
B05| 20| 60| Burst specialist
B06| 55| 25| Heavy attacker
B07| 45| 35| Controlled attacker
B08| 35| 45| Stability hybrid

Special identities:

- B01: Neutral baseline.
- B03: High burst-oriented offensive potential, but risky.
- B05: Anti-burst specialist.
- B06: Aggressive but relatively safer than B03.

Never make one blade universally superior.

---

6. DISC SYSTEM — MASS AND STABILITY

Disc statistics:

- MS = Mass
- ST = Stability

Conservation rule:

MS + ST = 100

Available discs:

Disc| MS| ST| Identity
D01| 50| 50| Balanced
D02| 65| 35| Heavy attacker support
D03| 80| 20| Extreme mass
D04| 35| 65| Defense-oriented
D05| 20| 80| Ultra stability
D06| 70| 30| Pressure build
D07| 60| 40| Hybrid
D08| 40| 60| Controlled defense

Special identities:

- D03: High pressure potential, low stability.
- D05: Stabilizer with reduced recoil.
- D06: Aggressive weight distribution.
- D04 and D08: Defensive anchors.

---

7. TIP SYSTEM — MOBILITY AND STAMINA

Tip statistics:

- MB = Mobility
- SM = Stamina

Conservation rule:

MB + SM = 100

Available tips:

Tip| MB| SM| Identity
T01| 50| 50| Balanced
T02| 70| 30| Attack mobility
T03| 85| 15| Extreme speed
T04| 30| 70| Stamina focus
T05| 15| 85| Ultra stamina
T06| 60| 40| Hybrid attacker
T07| 40| 60| Defensive stamina
T08| 75| 25| Unstable attacker

Special identities:

- T03: Fast, unstable chaos generator.
- T05: Endurance specialist.
- T02 and T08: Aggressive mobility.
- T07: Defensive stamina balance.

---

PART III — STAT SYSTEM

8. RESULTING BEYBLADE STATISTICS

A constructed Beyblade has six primary statistics:

Abbreviation| Full Name| Source
AP| Attack Power| Blade
LI| Lock Integrity| Blade
MS| Mass| Disc
ST| Stability| Disc
MB| Mobility| Tip
SM| Stamina| Tip

All six statistics are determined entirely by component selection.

No independent stat allocation is permitted.

9. AUTOMATIC TYPE CLASSIFICATION

Do not allow players to manually select their Beyblade type.

Type classification must emerge from the assembled components.

Initial classification rules:

Attack Type

- AP and MB are dominant.

Example: B03 + D02 + T02.

Defense Type

- ST and MS are dominant.

Example: B05 + D05 + T07.

Stamina Type

- SM is dominant.

Example: B04 + D04 + T05.

Balance Type

- No specific specialization is dominant.

Example: B01 + D01 + T01.

Develop a deterministic classification algorithm using normalized stat contributions.

Important: Because the six stats originate from three independent complementary pairs, avoid comparing raw values from unrelated scales without normalization.

Allow hybrid identities where appropriate, but assign one primary type for the initial combat system.

---

PART IV — COMBAT ENGINE

10. MATCH STRUCTURE

Each battle should last approximately 20–30 dynamic turns.

Each turn follows this sequence:

1. Players select actions.
2. Resolve engagement probability.
3. Determine whether a collision occurs.
4. Calculate collision impact.
5. Apply damage, recoil, and pressure.
6. Update energy and special meter.
7. Apply environmental effects.
8. Update player states and combat history.
9. Check victory conditions.
10. Display the updated battle state.

A match should end immediately when a valid victory condition is triggered.

11. PLAYER STATE

Each player has static and dynamic variables.

Static Variables

- AP
- ST
- SM
- MB
- MS
- LI
- Beyblade type

Dynamic Variables

- energy
- stability_level
- position_pressure
- passive_pressure
- special_meter (0–100)
- guard_stack
- dodge_stack
- combo_count
- last_action
- repeat_count

All dynamic variables must be maintained independently for each player.

Initialize them consistently at the beginning of every match.

---

PART V — ACTION SYSTEM

12. AVAILABLE ACTIONS

Players can choose one of five actions per turn.

A. ATTACK

Purpose:

- Maximize offensive impact.
- Increase collision probability.
- Generate pressure.

Multiplier:

Attack impact × 1.5

Engagement modifier: +0.15

B. DEFEND

Purpose:

- Reduce incoming impact.
- Preserve stability.
- Resist aggressive opponents.

Incoming impact multiplier:

× 0.6

Defense fatigue applies through guard_stack.

C. DODGE

Purpose:

- Avoid collisions.
- Reduce incoming offensive effectiveness.

Outgoing impact multiplier:

× 0.7

Engagement modifier:

−0.25 × dodge effectiveness

Repeated dodging must progressively lose effectiveness.

D. CHARGE

Purpose:

- Build special meter.
- Prepare a powerful offensive action.

Impact multiplier:

× 0.5

Special meter gain:

+15

Stamina-type bonus:

+25% charge gain.

Risks:

- Incoming damage × 1.25.
- Burst risk × 1.2.

E. SPECIAL

Available when:

special_meter ≥ 100

Special impact multiplier:

× 5.0

After activation:

special_meter = 0

Special attacks must involve substantial recoil and exposure risks.

The special attack must not become an automatic winning move.

---

PART VI — ENGAGEMENT AND COLLISION

13. COLLISION PROBABILITY

Base collision probability:

P = 0.4 + (MB₁ + MB₂)/200

Action modifiers:

- ATTACK: +0.15
- DODGE: −0.25 × dodge effectiveness
- Other actions: No direct modifier.

Clamp final probability:

0.2 ≤ P ≤ 0.9

Implement probability calculations carefully and consistently.

The result must be generated independently of any player-controlled manipulation of random numbers.

14. PASSIVE PRESSURE

Purpose: Prevent infinite stalling.

If no collision occurs:

passive_pressure += 3

When a collision occurs:

position_pressure += passive_pressure

passive_pressure = 0

Passive pressure must be assigned according to a clearly defined target and direction. Do not accidentally grant both players the same offensive advantage.

15. BASE IMPACT

Base impact:

Impact = AP × (1 + MB/120)

Apply the relevant action multipliers.

Apply type bonuses and specialization modifiers.

Introduce controlled randomness:

Random multiplier = random(0.9, 1.1)

Randomness must remain small relative to the influence of player decisions.

16. TYPE SYNERGY

Apply the following initial type bonuses:

Type| Bonus
Attack| +15% attack effectiveness
Defense| −20% incoming damage while defending; −15% recoil
Stamina| −20% energy drain; +25% charge gain
Balance| +5% all relevant combat efficiencies

Ensure bonuses do not accidentally stack multiple times or apply to unrelated calculations.

17. SPECIALIZATION SCALING

Use threshold-based bonuses.

Stat| Threshold| Bonus
AP| >50| +0.6% attack effectiveness per point
ST| >70| +0.5% resistance per point
SM| >70| −0.4% energy drain per point
MB| >70| +0.5% collision rate per point
MS| >70| +0.5% ring-out resistance per point
LI| >50| +0.7% burst resistance per point

These are proposed coefficients, not immutable laws.

Test their actual effects before finalizing them.

Avoid unbounded multipliers or unintended exponential scaling.

18. MOMENTUM

When:

combo_count ≥ 2

Apply:

- +5% impact per combo stack.
- Maximum impact bonus: +15%.
- +5% recoil per combo stack.

Define exactly when combos increase, reset, and expire.

Momentum must reward offensive consistency without creating an unstoppable snowball effect.

19. INITIATIVE BONUS

When an opponent uses DODGE or CHARGE:

Apply:

- +8% impact.
- +5 percentage points to burst probability.

This should reward reading the opponent's decisions.

Do not reveal the opponent's selected action before both players have submitted their moves.

---

PART VII — COLLISION RESOLUTION

20. COLLISION CALCULATIONS

When a collision occurs, calculate:

A. Stability Damage

StabilityLoss = Impact / ST

B. Recoil

Recoil = Impact / ST_self

C. Position Pressure

position_pressure += Impact / MS

D. Burst Check

Initial formula:

BurstChance = Impact × (MS / LI)

Modifiers:

- Charging opponent: ×1.2.
- Initiative: +5 percentage points.

E. Energy Loss

energy -= Impact / 20

IMPORTANT:

These are initial proposed formulas.

The implementation must convert burst calculations into valid probabilities between 0 and 1.

A raw quantity such as Impact × (MS / LI) must not be treated directly as a probability.

Likewise, prevent division by zero and extreme numerical instability.

Use suitable nonlinear probability functions, normalization, or calibrated coefficients.

All damage and resistance calculations must be tested against every component combination.

---

PART VIII — ENERGY AND FATIGUE

21. ENERGY SYSTEM

Initial energy:

energy = SM × 1.2

Passive drain per turn:

energy -= 1 + MB/80

Stamina type:

Passive drain × 0.8

Pressure drain:

If pressure > 70:

energy -= pressure / 50

Energy must never silently become negative without triggering the appropriate loss condition.

22. DEFENSE FATIGUE

Every consecutive DEFEND action:

guard_stack += 1

Damage reduction:

reduction = 20% − (5% × guard_stack)

Minimum reduction:

5%

Reset guard_stack after a non-defensive action.

Clarify whether the first defensive action starts at 15% or 20%, and implement one consistent convention.

23. DODGE DECAY

Every consecutive DODGE:

dodge_stack += 1

Dodge effectiveness decreases by 10% per stack.

Ensure effectiveness cannot become negative.

Reset or recover dodge effectiveness when the player changes strategy according to a clearly defined rule.

24. CHARGE SYSTEM

Each CHARGE action:

special_meter += 15

Stamina type:

+25% additional charge gain.

Apply the incoming damage and burst-risk penalties specified earlier.

Special meter must never exceed 100.

---

PART IX — ARENA AND ADAPTATION

25. ARENA DESTABILIZATION

Every turn:

global_instability += 1

Effective stability decreases by 0.5% per turn.

Implement this as a clearly defined multiplicative or additive decay model.

Avoid allowing arena instability to produce negative stability.

The arena should gradually become more dangerous, encouraging decisive play.

26. ADAPTATION BONUS

If a player breaks an established repetition pattern:

Next action effectiveness += 5%

Define repetition detection precisely.

The system should distinguish between:

- Repeated actions.
- Repeated action sequences.
- Strategic changes.

Do not award the bonus merely for alternating actions without meaningful strategic context.

27. SPECIALIZATION IDENTITY

If a dominant stat is at least 1.25 times the relevant comparison statistics:

Apply:

+8% domain efficiency.

The comparison method must be mathematically defined and consistent across all six statistics.

Avoid double-counting this bonus with existing type synergy and specialization scaling.

---

PART X — WIN CONDITIONS

28. THREE VICTORY CONDITIONS

A. BURST FINISH

If a Beyblade bursts:

Immediate defeat.

Lock Integrity, incoming impact, mass, and relevant resistance modifiers determine burst probability.

B. RING-OUT

If:

pressure > 120

Trigger a ring-out probability check.

Ring-out resistance must depend on the appropriate defensive statistics.

C. SPIN FINISH

If:

energy ≤ 0

The Beyblade stops spinning and loses.

The system should determine simultaneous defeat conditions and draw scenarios consistently.

---

PART XI — STRATEGIC IDENTITIES

29. EXPECTED COMBAT ARCHETYPES

Attack Builds:

- High burst potential.
- High offensive impact.
- Vulnerable to recoil and instability.

Defense Builds:

- High stability and mass-based resistance.
- Strong defensive potential.
- Vulnerable to passive pressure and prolonged exposure.

Stamina Builds:

- Efficient energy management.
- Strong long-game potential.
- Vulnerable to sustained pressure and burst threats.

Balance Builds:

- Versatile.
- Fewer extreme weaknesses.
- Potentially outperformed by specialists in their respective domains.

These are strategic tendencies, not guaranteed outcomes.

---

PART XII — TELEGRAM IMPLEMENTATION

30. PLATFORM

The game must be implemented as a Telegram Bot.

Required commands:

/start
/help
/build
/challenge @username

Additional commands may be introduced when useful.

31. MATCH FLOW

1. Player A challenges Player B.
2. Player B receives a challenge notification.
3. Player B accepts or rejects.
4. Both players select their Beyblade builds.
5. The match initializes.
6. Both players receive action controls.
7. Players submit their actions.
8. The server resolves the turn.
9. The battle interface updates.
10. The process repeats until a victory condition is reached.
11. Both players receive the final result.

32. TELEGRAM UI

Use an interactive, clean interface.

Preferred implementation:

- One main battle message per player.
- Edit existing messages after each turn.
- Inline keyboard buttons for actions.
- Clear visual representation of both Beyblades.
- Display relevant combat statistics.
- Show energy, stability, pressure, and special meter.
- Provide readable combat logs.
- Indicate whose turn is pending.

Avoid flooding the Telegram chat with separate messages for every action.

33. ACTION CALLBACK

Use a structured callback format:

action:{match_id}:{player_id}:{move}

Validate every callback on the server.

Never trust client-provided player identities, match states, or combat results.

34. TIMEOUT SYSTEM

Turn timeout:

60 seconds.

If a player fails to submit an action:

Automatically choose between:

- DEFEND
- DODGE

The selection should be controlled by a documented deterministic or probabilistic fallback rule.

Prevent players from intentionally exploiting timeouts.

---

PART XIII — DATA ARCHITECTURE

35. USER MODEL

Suggested structure:

{
user_id,
builds: [],
default_build_id
}

Each build should contain:

{
build_id,
core_id,
blade_id,
disc_id,
tip_id,
display_name,
created_at
}

All numerical statistics should be generated from the selected components, not independently edited by users.

36. MATCH MODEL

Suggested structure:

{
match_id,
players,
states,
step,
message_id,
pending_actions,
status,
created_at,
updated_at
}

Include all necessary information to recover a match after server restarts.

37. CONCURRENCY

Critical rule:

ONE MATCH = ONE LOCK.

Only one turn-resolution operation may execute for a match at a time.

Implement:

- Atomic action submission.
- Duplicate callback protection.
- Idempotent turn resolution.
- Race-condition prevention.
- Timeout handling.
- Match recovery after crashes.

Two players submitting simultaneously must not cause duplicate or inconsistent turn resolution.

---

PART XIV — GAME BALANCING AND VALIDATION

38. MANDATORY SIMULATION TESTING

Before declaring the game balanced, run automated simulations.

Test:

1. Every Beyblade component individually.
2. Every possible combination where computationally feasible.
3. Every major archetype against every other archetype.
4. Aggressive versus defensive strategies.
5. Stamina versus attack strategies.
6. Repeated DEFEND.
7. Repeated DODGE.
8. Repeated CHARGE.
9. Special attack timing.
10. Timeout exploitation.
11. Maximum pressure scenarios.
12. Extreme-stat configurations.

The construction system has 7,680 possible builds, making exhaustive build evaluation feasible for an appropriately optimized simulator.

Run many battles using different random seeds.

39. BALANCE METRICS

Track:

- Win rate by build.
- Win rate by archetype.
- Average match duration.
- Burst finish frequency.
- Ring-out frequency.
- Spin finish frequency.
- Average energy remaining.
- Action selection frequency.
- Most successful action sequences.
- Frequency of defensive stalling.
- Special attack success rate.

Identify:

- Dominant builds.
- Dominant actions.
- Exploitable combinations.
- Unintended infinite loops.
- Overpowered specialization bonuses.

A 50% win rate is not required for every individual build, but no build or action should be overwhelmingly superior across opponents and situations.

40. DESIGN VALIDATION RULES

Preserve these principles:

- AP + LI = 80.
- MS + ST = 100.
- MB + SM = 100.
- Cores remain cosmetic.
- Every component must have meaningful trade-offs.
- No component should be strictly superior.
- No unlimited defensive strategy.
- No unlimited special attacks.
- No uncontrolled randomness.
- No pay-to-win advantages.

Do not introduce rarity, upgrades, or stat boosts in the initial version.

---

PART XV — FUTURE EXPANSION

41. COMPONENT EXPANSION

New components may be added without changing the fundamental architecture.

Example:

B09 → AP: 65 | LI: 15

B10 → AP: 25 | LI: 55

Every new blade must satisfy:

AP + LI = 80

Likewise, all future discs and tips must satisfy their respective conservation rules.

The database and code architecture must support adding new components through configuration or database records rather than rewriting the combat engine.

42. FUTURE FEATURES

D

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

Stamina Type

- SM is dominant.

Example: B04 + D04 + T05.

Balance Type

- No specific specialization is dominant.

Example: B01 + D01 + T01.

Develop a deterministic classification algorithm using normalized stat contributions.

Important: Because the six stats originate from three independent complementary pairs, avoid comparing raw values from unrelated scales without normalization.

Allow hybrid identities where appropriate, but assign one primary type for the initial combat system.

---

PART IV — COMBAT ENGINE

10. MATCH STRUCTURE

Each battle should last approximately 20–30 dynamic turns.

Each turn follows this sequence:

1. Players select actions.
2. Resolve engagement probability.
3. Determine whether a collision occurs.
4. Calculate collision impact.
5. Apply damage, recoil, and pressure.
6. Update energy and special meter.
7. Apply environmental effects.
8. Update player states and combat history.
9. Check victory conditions.
10. Display the updated battle state.

A match should end immediately when a valid victory condition is triggered.

11. PLAYER STATE

Each player has static and dynamic variables.

Static Variables

- AP
- ST
- SM
- MB
- MS
- LI
- Beyblade type

Dynamic Variables

- energy
- stability_level
- position_pressure
- passive_pressure
- special_meter (0–100)
- guard_stack
- dodge_stack
- combo_count
- last_action
- repeat_count

All dynamic variables must be maintained independently for each player.

Initialize them consistently at the beginning of every match.

---

PART V — ACTION SYSTEM

12. AVAILABLE ACTIONS

Players can choose one of five actions per turn.

A. ATTACK

Purpose:

- Maximize offensive impact.
- Increase collision probability.
- Generate pressure.

Multiplier:

Attack impact × 1.5

Engagement modifier: +0.15

B. DEFEND

Purpose:

- Reduce incoming impact.
- Preserve stability.
- Resist aggressive opponents.

Incoming impact multiplier:

× 0.6

Defense fatigue applies through guard_stack.

C. DODGE

Purpose:

- Avoid collisions.
- Reduce incoming offensive effectiveness.

Outgoing impact multiplier:

× 0.7

Engagement modifier:

−0.25 × dodge effectiveness

Repeated dodging must progressively lose effectiveness.

D. CHARGE

Purpose:

- Build special meter.
- Prepare a powerful offensive action.

Impact multiplier:

× 0.5

Special meter gain:

+15

Stamina-type bonus:

+25% charge gain.

Risks:

- Incoming damage × 1.25.
- Burst risk × 1.2.

E. SPECIAL

Available when:

special_meter ≥ 100

Special impact multiplier:

× 5.0

After activation:

special_meter = 0

Special attacks must involve substantial recoil and exposure risks.

The special attack must not become an automatic winning move.

---

PART VI — ENGAGEMENT AND COLLISION

13. COLLISION PROBABILITY

Base collision probability:

P = 0.4 + (MB₁ + MB₂)/200

Action modifiers:

- ATTACK: +0.15
- DODGE: −0.25 × dodge effectiveness
- Other actions: No direct modifier.

Clamp final probability:

0.2 ≤ P ≤ 0.9

Implement probability calculations carefully and consistently.

The result must be generated independently of any player-controlled manipulation of random numbers.

14. PASSIVE PRESSURE

Purpose: Prevent infinite stalling.

If no collision occurs:

passive_pressure += 3

When a collision occurs:

position_pressure += passive_pressure

passive_pressure = 0

Passive pressure must be assigned according to a clearly defined target and direction. Do not accidentally grant both players the same offensive advantage.

15. BASE IMPACT

Base impact:

Impact = AP × (1 + MB/120)

Apply the relevant action multipliers.

Apply type bonuses and specialization modifiers.

Introduce controlled randomness:

Random multiplier = random(0.9, 1.1)

Randomness must remain small relative to the influence of player decisions.

16. TYPE SYNERGY

Apply the following initial type bonuses:

Type| Bonus
Attack| +15% attack effectiveness
Defense| −20% incoming damage while defending; −15% recoil
Stamina| −20% energy drain; +25% charge gain
Balance| +5% all relevant combat efficiencies

Ensure bonuses do not accidentally stack multiple times or apply to unrelated calculations.

17. SPECIALIZATION SCALING

Use threshold-based bonuses.

Stat| Threshold| Bonus
AP| >50| +0.6% attack effectiveness per point
ST| >70| +0.5% resistance per point
SM| >70| −0.4% energy drain per point
MB| >70| +0.5% collision rate per point
MS| >70| +0.5% ring-out resistance per point
LI| >50| +0.7% burst resistance per point

These are proposed coefficients, not immutable laws.

Test their actual effects before finalizing them.

Avoid unbounded multipliers or unintended exponential scaling.

18. MOMENTUM

When:

combo_count ≥ 2

Apply:

- +5% impact per combo stack.
- Maximum impact bonus: +15%.
- +5% recoil per combo stack.

Define exactly when combos increase, reset, and expire.

Momentum must reward offensive consistency without creating an unstoppable snowball effect.

19. INITIATIVE BONUS

When an opponent uses DODGE or CHARGE:

Apply:

- +8% impact.
- +5 percentage points to burst probability.

This should reward reading the opponent's decisions.

Do not reveal the opponent's selected action before both players have submitted their moves.

---

PART VII — COLLISION RESOLUTION

20. COLLISION CALCULATIONS

When a collision occurs, calculate:

A. Stability Damage

StabilityLoss = Impact / ST

B. Recoil

Recoil = Impact / ST_self

C. Position Pressure

position_pressure += Impact / MS

D. Burst Check

Initial formula:

BurstChance = Impact × (MS / LI)

Modifiers:

- Charging opponent: ×1.2.
- Initiative: +5 percentage points.

E. Energy Loss

energy -= Impact / 20

IMPORTANT:

These are initial proposed formulas.

The implementation must convert burst calculations into valid probabilities between 0 and 1.

A raw quantity such as Impact × (MS / LI) must not be treated directly as a probability.

Likewise, prevent division by zero and extreme numerical instability.

Use suitable nonlinear probability functions, normalization, or calibrated coefficients.

All damage and resistance calculations must be tested against every component combination.

---

PART VIII — ENERGY AND FATIGUE

21. ENERGY SYSTEM

Initial energy:

energy = SM × 1.2

Passive drain per turn:

energy -= 1 + MB/80

Stamina type:

Passive drain × 0.8

Pressure drain:

If pressure > 70:

energy -= pressure / 50

Energy must never silently become negative without triggering the appropriate loss condition.

22. DEFENSE FATIGUE

Every consecutive DEFEND action:

guard_stack += 1

Damage reduction:

reduction = 20% − (5% × guard_stack)

Minimum reduction:

5%

Reset guard_stack after a non-defensive action.

Clarify whether the first defensive action starts at 15% or 20%, and implement one consistent convention.

23. DODGE DECAY

Every consecutive DODGE:

dodge_stack += 1

Dodge effectiveness decreases by 10% per stack.

Ensure effectiveness cannot become negative.

Reset or recover dodge effectiveness when the player changes strategy according to a clearly defined rule.

24. CHARGE SYSTEM

Each CHARGE action:

special_meter += 15

Stamina type:

+25% additional charge gain.

Apply the incoming damage and burst-risk penalties specified earlier.

Special meter must never exceed 100.

---

PART IX — ARENA AND ADAPTATION

25. ARENA DESTABILIZATION

Every turn:

global_instability += 1

Effective stability decreases by 0.5% per turn.

Implement this as a clearly defined multiplicative or additive decay model.

Avoid allowing arena instability to produce negative stability.

The arena should gradually become more dangerous, encouraging decisive play.

26. ADAPTATION BONUS

If a player breaks an established repetition pattern:

Next action effectiveness += 5%

Define repetition detection precisely.

The system should distinguish between:

- Repeated actions.
- Repeated action sequences.
- Strategic changes.

Do not award the bonus merely for alternating actions without meaningful strategic context.

27. SPECIALIZATION IDENTITY

If a dominant stat is at least 1.25 times the relevant comparison statistics:

Apply:

+8% domain efficiency.

The comparison method must be mathematically defined and consistent across all six statistics.

Avoid double-counting this bonus with existing type synergy and specialization scaling.

---

PART X — WIN CONDITIONS

28. THREE VICTORY CONDITIONS

A. BURST FINISH

If a Beyblade bursts:

Immediate defeat.

Lock Integrity, incoming impact, mass, and relevant resistance modifiers determine burst probability.

B. RING-OUT

If:

pressure > 120

Trigger a ring-out probability check.

Ring-out resistance must depend on the appropriate defensive statistics.

C. SPIN FINISH

If:

energy ≤ 0

The Beyblade stops spinning and loses.

The system should determine simultaneous defeat conditions and draw scenarios consistently.

---

PART XI — STRATEGIC IDENTITIES

29. EXPECTED COMBAT ARCHETYPES

Attack Builds:

- High burst potential.
- High offensive impact.
- Vulnerable to recoil and instability.

Defense Builds:

- High stability and mass-based resistance.
- Strong defensive potential.
- Vulnerable to passive pressure and prolonged exposure.

Stamina Builds:

- Efficient energy management.
- Strong long-game potential.
- Vulnerable to sustained pressure and burst threats.

Balance Builds:

- Versatile.
- Fewer extreme weaknesses.
- Potentially outperformed by specialists in their respective domains.

These are strategic tendencies, not guaranteed outcomes.

---

PART XII — TELEGRAM IMPLEMENTATION

30. PLATFORM

The game must be implemented as a Telegram Bot.

Required commands:

/start
/help
/build
/challenge @username

Additional commands may be introduced when useful.

31. MATCH FLOW

1. Player A challenges Player B.
2. Player B receives a challenge notification.
3. Player B accepts or rejects.
4. Both players select their Beyblade builds.
5. The match initializes.
6. Both players receive action controls.
7. Players submit their actions.
8. The server resolves the turn.
9. The battle interface updates.
10. The process repeats until a victory condition is reached.
11. Both players receive the final result.

32. TELEGRAM UI

Use an interactive, clean interface.

Preferred implementation:

- One main battle message per player.
- Edit existing messages after each turn.
- Inline keyboard buttons for actions.
- Clear visual representation of both Beyblades.
- Display relevant combat statistics.
- Show energy, stability, pressure, and special meter.
- Provide readable combat logs.
- Indicate whose turn is pending.

Avoid flooding the Telegram chat with separate messages for every action.

33. ACTION CALLBACK

Use a structured callback format:

action:{match_id}:{player_id}:{move}

Validate every callback on the server.

Never trust client-provided player identities, match states, or combat results.

34. TIMEOUT SYSTEM

Turn timeout:

60 seconds.

If a player fails to submit an action:

Automatically choose between:

- DEFEND
- DODGE

The selection should be controlled by a documented deterministic or probabilistic fallback rule.

Prevent players from intentionally exploiting timeouts.

---

PART XIII — DATA ARCHITECTURE

35. USER MODEL

Suggested structure:

{
user_id,
builds: [],
default_build_id
}

Each build should contain:

{
build_id,
core_id,
blade_id,
disc_id,
tip_id,
display_name,
created_at
}

All numerical statistics should be generated from the selected components, not independently edited by users.

36. MATCH MODEL

Suggested structure:

{
match_id,
players,
states,
step,
message_id,
pending_actions,
status,
created_at,
updated_at
}

Include all necessary information to recover a match after server restarts.

37. CONCURRENCY

Critical rule:

ONE MATCH = ONE LOCK.

Only one turn-resolution operation may execute for a match at a time.

Implement:

- Atomic action submission.
- Duplicate callback protection.
- Idempotent turn resolution.
- Race-condition prevention.
- Timeout handling.
- Match recovery after crashes.

Two players submitting simultaneously must not cause duplicate or inconsistent turn resolution.

---

PART XIV — GAME BALANCING AND VALIDATION

38. MANDATORY SIMULATION TESTING

Before declaring the game balanced, run automated simulations.

Test:

1. Every Beyblade component individually.
2. Every possible combination where computationally feasible.
3. Every major archetype against every other archetype.
4. Aggressive versus defensive strategies.
5. Stamina versus attack strategies.
6. Repeated DEFEND.
7. Repeated DODGE.
8. Repeated CHARGE.
9. Special attack timing.
10. Timeout exploitation.
11. Maximum pressure scenarios.
12. Extreme-stat configurations.

The construction system has 7,680 possible builds, making exhaustive build evaluation feasible for an appropriately optimized simulator.

Run many battles using different random seeds.

39. BALANCE METRICS

Track:

- Win rate by build.
- Win rate by archetype.
- Average match duration.
- Burst finish frequency.
- Ring-out frequency.
- Spin finish frequency.
- Average energy remaining.
- Action selection frequency.
- Most successful action sequences.
- Frequency of defensive stalling.
- Special attack success rate.

Identify:

- Dominant builds.
- Dominant actions.
- Exploitable combinations.
- Unintended infinite loops.
- Overpowered specialization bonuses.

A 50% win rate is not required for every individual build, but no build or action should be overwhelmingly superior across opponents and situations.

40. DESIGN VALIDATION RULES

Preserve these principles:

- AP + LI = 80.
- MS + ST = 100.
- MB + SM = 100.
- Cores remain cosmetic.
- Every component must have meaningful trade-offs.
- No component should be strictly superior.
- No unlimited defensive strategy.
- No unlimited special attacks.
- No uncontrolled randomness.
- No pay-to-win advantages.

Do not introduce rarity, upgrades, or stat boosts in the initial version.

---

PART XV — FUTURE EXPANSION

41. COMPONENT EXPANSION

New components may be added without changing the fundamental architecture.

Example:

B09 → AP: 65 | LI: 15

B10 → AP: 25 | LI: 55

Every new blade must satisfy:

AP + LI = 80

Likewise, all future discs and tips must satisfy their respective conservation rules.

The database and code architecture must support adding new components through configuration or database records rather than rewriting the combat engine.

42. FUTURE FEATURES

D

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

- **High — stale turn timers can play extra moves or affect a rematch.** In [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js:231-255`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js), each resolved turn schedules a 60-second timeout, but submitting a move does not cancel that timeout. If it fires just after the move resolves, `submitted` is already `false`, so it can resolve an unintended `DEFEND` turn. Older timeouts also survive when a new match launches and can act on that match. **Fix:** clear the pending timer when a move is submitted and before launching a match; maintain exactly one timeout per active turn, and invalidate callbacks from prior matches.

- **Medium — stability loss does not weaken combat performance.** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/engine.mjs:219-220, 247-248`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/engine.mjs) calculate stability loss, but incoming stability loss uses the Bey’s original `st` stat rather than its current `fighter.stability`. Current stability otherwise only affects the turn-limit score, so the displayed meter has no effect on combat before the limit. **Fix:** derive the effective stability factor from current fighter stability, with a safe minimum.

## Spin//Forge

A standalone, browser-playable Beyblade-inspired forge and arena. Build combinations from four parts, then battle an AI rival with simultaneous hidden actions and deterministic seeded combat.

### Run locally

Requires Node.js 20+ for the tests and Python 3 for the static web server. From the project root:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 3002
```

Open <http://localhost:3002>. No package installation or build step is required. To stop the server, press `Ctrl+C`.

### Tests

```sh
node --test engine.test.mjs
node --check app.js
node --check engine.mjs
```

The engine test suite validates all 7,680 part combinations, stat-pair conservation, invalid actions and special-meter requirements, and repeated/adaptive strategy match simulations.

### Gameplay notes

- Cores change appearance and identity only; combat stats come from the blade, disc, and tip.
- Stat pairs are conserved: AP + LI = 80, MS + ST = 100, and MB + SM = 100.
- The forge classifies type deterministically from the assembled stats. In the arena, both fighters choose simultaneously; the rival's move is hidden until resolution.
- Combat has controlled seeded randomness. It is an abstract strategy simulation, not a real-time physics model.
- Saved builds use this browser's local storage; they are not synced between devices.

### Telegram integration boundary

This repository currently contains only the standalone browser game. It does not include a Telegram bot, server-side match authority, database, or deployment configuration. A Telegram release still needs a bot token and deployment target, plus server-side challenge and private-action flows, persisted player/build/match state, turn deadlines, and concurrency/idempotency protections. Keep the token in deployment secrets; never put it in browser code or commit it to the repository.

+A standalone, browser-playable Beyblade-inspired forge and arena. Build combinations from four parts, then battle an AI rival with simultaneous hidden actions and deterministic seeded combat.
+
+### Run locally
+
+Requires Node.js 20+ for the tests and Python 3 for the static web server. From the project root:
+
+```sh
+python3 -m http.server 3002
+```
+
+Open <http://localhost:3002>. No package installation or build step is required. To stop the server, press `Ctrl+C`.
+
+### Tests
+
+```sh
+node --test engine.test.mjs
+node --check app.js
+node --check engine.mjs
+```
+
+The engine test suite validates all 7,680 part combinations, stat-pair conservation, invalid actions and special-meter requirements, and repeated/adaptive strategy match simulations.
+
+### Gameplay notes
+
+- Cores change appearance and identity only; combat stats come from the blade, disc, and tip.
+- Stat pairs are conserved: AP + LI = 80, MS + ST = 100, and MB + SM = 100.
+- The forge classifies type deterministically from the assembled stats. In the arena, both fighters choose simultaneously; the rival's move is hidden until resolution.
+- Combat has controlled seeded randomness. It is an abstract strategy simulation, not a real-time physics model.
+- Saved builds use this browser's local storage; they are not synced between devices.
+
+### Telegram integration boundary
+
+This repository currently contains only the standalone browser game. It does not include a Telegram bot, server-side match authority, database, or deployment configuration. A Telegram release still needs a bot token and deployment target, plus server-side challenge and private-action flows, persisted player/build/match state, turn deadlines, and concurrency/idempotency protections. Keep the token in deployment secrets; never put it in browser code or commit it to the repository.
